Definition: second person imperative present of G1510; be thou:--+ agree, be, X give thyself wholly to.
BiblicalUsage: Be thou is the command Jesus gives, and it lands like a word spoken straight to one person. In Matthew 5:25 he says, agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him, in Mark 5:34 he tells the woman, daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole, go in peace, and be whole of thy plague, and in Luke 19:17 the nobleman says to his servant, well, thou good servant, because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the little command carries the whole gospel: agree, be whole, and have authority, all because he spoke it.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; Jairus' Daughter and the Bleeding Woman; The Parable of the Talents
